decision: Do not integrate any cloud-height-bound variant. All production code is restored exactly. The .7 Windows/Linux archives remain current and unchanged.
scope: Scratch-only optimization of existing volume density queries; no resolution/sample-count/default/settings/geometry/engine changes were accepted.
design: Profile support is bounded analytically: stratus [0,.13], cumulus [.075,.755], nimbus [.02,1] of the 2200..5800 layer. Skip known-empty density samples before six weather/type texture reads, leaving all ray-march sample positions and shadow quadrature intact.

The initial variant publishes a conservative union as one vec2 global. A surface-only variant leaves sky source byte-identical. A third variant tests the existing weather type in each density query. The last variant sets a pure-cumulus flag once per frame in the previously unused storm.w component, without adding a global uniform.
The pure-cumulus variants retain the original guard for all other weather. Their extra conditional still produces a measured mixed-weather cost; correctness alone does not justify adoption.
findings: The initial fair High sky comparison is exact and about 13.4% faster, but mixed High changes 5073 of 8294400 pixels (peak 23/255). Subsequent candidate held/repeat controls sometimes switch between the same two images. Original-only 4K High control passes 19/0. No cause is established; longer settling and preserving the original guard did not establish strict parity.

Direct GPU comparisons of density and shadows pass in Forward+ and Mobile. The generic surface candidate passes 99-check volume/lifecycle suites per backend. These results do not cure the separate sky or timing failures.
General surface bounds save about 6.1% on the fair ground view and 7.1% on fair water. Mixed-water GPU time increases about 4.3%, and clearing/storm bring no useful gain.
The runtime type check retains exact fair/mixed surface images, but mixed ground and water are slower by about 2.6% and 6.3%.

The final per-frame flag passes 136 assertions, including 3538944 GPU sample positions and all four 4K ground/water fair/mixed image controls. It saves about 5.4% on fair ground and 7.3% on fair water, while mixed ground/water cost increases about 1.8%/2.5%. That tradeoff does not address the reported expensive mixed-weather workload.

environment.method: ABBA; each arm follows game time 424.2666667..430.25 after 256 warmup frames, then 360 measured normal frames. Use viewport GPU timestamps. Both shader programs prewarm before measuring. Clock, process and image records are retained per run. Clocks are not locked; no driver/display/unrelated process changes.
environment.ground_scene: Original bz2g terrain, orthographic 60m span around (64,64), Detailed terrain, Ingos cloud/weather parameters. This is not a complete Ingos LMP scene.
environment.water_scene: Original zone1 terrain/water, low camera; sunlight attenuation disabled to isolate reflected volume work.
environment.gpu_residency: Desktop rendering remains on GPU0. GPU1 has inactive ComfyUI and small Xorg allocations; dmon/pmon record activity. Other Godot engine observations are retained, not omitted.

limits: These are isolated viewport timings, not whole-game FPS or Windows RTX4090 Mobile results. The Windows 9 FPS report remains unresolved.
Initial 1440 fair01 had a backwards clock step between warmup and timing/capture. Preserve as exploratory only; exclude from performance conclusions.

clearing4k01 overlapped a headless import/export. mixed-integrated4k01 and density-forward01 have brief other-engine observations; they are not clean-device timing evidence. Final candidate04 cost runs have no other Godot engine observations.

Final frame-flag storm/clearing, Mobile and wider gameplay validation were not pursued after the mixed-weather slowdown was established; prior variant results are not inherited as final-candidate acceptance.
No user save, game data, public release, Windows runtime, graphics defaults or local package was changed. No subagents were used.
